reason: Alder & Finch (assigned provider, event-007/008) sent invoice NBL-019-INV-11 for £174 (event-014, remedial-works-invoice.pdf). The address and provider match the job. The only variation is the shortened address in event-002, which is not a real mismatch. However, we asked for a quotation only and told them not to start work until we issued written authority (event-008). Rowan said he misunderstood and had already done the work (event-013). The landlord's approval (event-005) was to proceed with the remedial works. It set no price and was given before any quote, so it does not clearly cover a specific amount. The £174 is below the £300 threshold but that is not an agency allowance. The invoice is a single lump sum with no itemisation, and there is no quote, no attendance date, no access details and no photos. The former tenant had returned the keys on 27 August (event-003) and the agency held a set, so how access was gained is unexplained. Completion is only the provider's claim, so I am not closing or paying, and I am not telling the landlord the work is done. I chose a specific question to the provider over escalation because the provider holds the missing facts. If the answers show unauthorised access or a dispute, or if the landlord questions the cost, route it to a person. Once the details are in, route the invoice to the landlord for approval of £174, or check completion with the landlord. The tenant has left, so the closing check on completion must come from the provider or landlord. No hazard is reported.
message:
Hello Rowan, thank you for sending invoice NBL-019-INV-11 (£174.00) for 18 Brindle Row. Before we can take it to the landlord, please send us the following:
1. An itemised breakdown of the £174.00 across the six items (floorboard and carpet, new Venetian blind, cupboard handle, kitchen blind, toilet seat, gate hinge), including materials and labour.
2. The date and time you attended, and how you got access to the property. The former tenant vacated on 27 August, and we had asked for inspection windows and access details first.
3. Any before and after photos of the work.
To confirm, our request was for a quotation only. No price has been agreed and no written authority to start work was issued. The invoice is not approved or payable at this stage. We will put it to the landlord once we have this information.
Kind regards,
Maya Chen, Northbridge Lettings
unknowns: Attendance date and how access was obtained
Whether work was actually completed (no photos)
Whether landlord accepts £174 without a prior quote
